# File System (fs)

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node-`fs`-shaped synchronous file I/O for reading/writing config, data, and logs — not `File`/`FileReader`/`FileSystemFileHandle` (those model browser sandbox/permission concepts that don't exist for a native CLI/microservice program with direct filesystem access).

**Coverage**: 19/20 (95%) · **Strict Coverage**: 2/20 (10%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |

| Async variants — callback (`fs.readFile(path, cb)`) + Promise (`fs.promises.readFile` / `import from 'fs/promises'`) | ✅ | • The `fs.promises` ops are genuinely non-blocking — `readFile`/`writeFile`/`appendFile`/`unlink`/`mkdir`/`rmdir`/`rename`/`copyFile`/`readdir` run on a background thread pool (default 4, `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE`) and return a pending Promise the loop settles on completion, so other connections/timers keep running during the I/O ([TDD-00185](../tdd/TDD-00185.md)/[ADR-00773](../adr/ADR-00773.md)/[ADR-00774](../adr/ADR-00774.md)). Two cases stay on the inline (delivery-only async, no concurrency gain — [TDD-00107](../tdd/TDD-00107.md)/[ADR-00340](../adr/ADR-00340.md)) path: the legacy **callback** form (`fs.readFile(path, cb)`), and a `writeFile`/`appendFile` whose data is an `ArrayBuffer`/`TypedArray` (its byte-length write). The pool is POSIX-first — Windows keeps the inline path pending the reactor work<br>• `readFile` delivers a string (text) — inherits `readFileSync`'s text-only caveat; no async binary (`Buffer`) form<br>• No `options`/`encoding` argument; no *async* `stat` (the sync `fs.statSync`/`lstatSync` exist — see the row above — but have no callback/Promise form yet) | • Covers the sync set: `readFile`/`writeFile`/`appendFile`/`unlink`/`mkdir`/`rmdir`/`rename`/`copyFile`/`readdir`. Callback gets `(err[, data])`; the Promise rejects with the same `Error` the sync form throws<br>• Reuses each `*Sync` runtime helper verbatim, catching its throw via the compiler's own `setjmp` catch primitive — no parallel non-throwing I/O code |
| `fs.createReadStream` / `fs.createWriteStream` | ✅ | • Chunks are **strings**, not `Buffer`s — text-first, like `readFileSync` (an embedded NUL truncates a chunk); binary (`Uint8Array`) streaming is a follow-on<br>• `createReadStream` reads on the background thread pool ([TDD-00186](../tdd/TDD-00186.md)/[ADR-00775](../adr/ADR-00775.md)) — the file is opened synchronously (a missing file still throws) then read off the loop thread, each highWaterMark chunk enqueued into the `Readable` in order, so the read no longer freezes the reactor. Consumer backpressure is not yet honored (the worker reads ahead and chunks queue in the readable — the same memory profile the eager path had); true highWaterMark backpressure is a follow-on. On Windows the pre-pool eager read-to-EOF fill is kept (the pool runtime is POSIX-only) pending the reactor work<br>• Options: `createReadStream` takes `{ highWaterMark }`, `createWriteStream` `{ flags: "w"\|"a" }` — both compile-time literals; `start`/`end`/`fd`/`encoding` are clean errors | • `createReadStream` returns a Node `Readable` (consumable via `for await` or `.on('data')`/`.on('end')`/`.pipe()`); `createWriteStream` a Node `Writable` (`.write`/`.end`, `'finish'`/`'close'`/`'drain'`). A read→write `.pipe()` round-trips. A failed open throws a catchable `Error` (like `readFileSync`) ([TDD-00108](../tdd/TDD-00108.md)/[ADR-00343](../adr/ADR-00343.md))<br>• Also wired `for await` over any Node `Readable` (was WHATWG-only) |
| `fs.watch(path, listener)` → `FSWatcher` | ✅ | • `filename` is faithful on Linux (inotify names the changed entry) but is the **watched path** on macOS — kqueue/`EVFILT_VNODE` watches an fd, not a directory's entries, so it cannot name a changed child (Node uses FSEvents there); a documented divergence, the file-watch case (the common one) is faithful ([ADR-00758](../adr/ADR-00758.md))<br>• One listener slot per event (`.on('change'|'rename', …)`, arrow-literal only) — the `Worker`/`ChildProcess` posture, not the full `EventEmitter`<br>• `recursive` is honoured natively where the OS supports it (macOS/Windows); on Linux (inotify) it watches only the named path — not the subtree<br>• `encoding` accepts only `'utf8'`; no coalescing/ordering guarantees (as in Node, event streams are platform-dependent) | • The faithful, event-driven watch — a native OS change source folded into the `select()` loop via the standard hook trio (keepalive/fdset/dispatch), no `stat`-poll. See [TDD-00181](../tdd/TDD-00181.md) / [ADR-00756](../adr/ADR-00756.md)–[ADR-00758](../adr/ADR-00758.md) |
| `File` / `FileReader` / `FileSystemFileHandle` (browser-flavored File API) | ❌ | | **Differentiator (scoped — [TDD-00172](../tdd/TDD-00172.md)).** Splits in two: the **data layer** (`File extends Blob`, `FileReader.readAsText`/`ArrayBuffer`/`DataURL`) is a thin fs-backed reinterpretation with no UI — path-backed `File`s, reads firing `onload` on the event loop; the **picker layer** (`showOpenFilePicker` → `FileSystemFileHandle`) resolves a path through a pluggable UI backend — a `klain:tui` file-picker widget, a `klain:webview` native dialog, or an explicit-path degradation when headless. Serves interactive native apps (TUI file managers/editors); the data layer is the near-term, standalone-useful piece. |
